intent_json.research_question: Among adults aged 18 years and older with two consecutive elevated office blood pressure measurements (SBP >= 130 mmHg OR DBP >= 80 mmHg per ACC/AHA 2017) within a 24-month window and no prior cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, thyroid disease, secondary hypertension, or antihypertensive exposure, does the latency from first elevated blood pressure to recorded hypertension diagnosis predict major adverse cardiovascular events (myocardial infarction, ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke, heart failure hospitalization, or all-cause death) and incident chronic kidney disease compared to a propensity-matched normotensive comparator? Secondary aims: (a) reproduce Lu 2025's reported 29 percent higher cardiovascular risk score among patients with diagnostic delay greater than 12 months; (b) characterize antihypertensive treatment trajectories from diagnosis through follow-up; (c) describe the class composition of apparent treatment-resistant hypertension (three or more antihypertensive classes with overlapping 30-day exposure) and renal-sympathetic-denervation eligibility; (d) measure baseline laboratory ordering frequency including CBC, CMP, lipid panel, TSH, and serum aldosterone within plus or minus 14 days of diagnosis, plus the conversion rate from aldosterone testing to documented primary aldosteronism diagnosis within 12 months. Target source: Acumenus OMOP CDM. Pre-registered Holm-Bonferroni correction; OHDSI EmpiricalCalibration on negative-control outcomes; 5-year primary censoring with all-available-follow-up as sensitivity.
known_gaps: AI-derived fields require review and canonical OHDSI asset verification.
